nonblocking_findings.finding: Residual left-boundary gap: the lookbehind excludes only `\w` (Unicode-aware, so accented/non-Latin letters are correctly covered) and ASCII hyphen-minus. `/`, `.`, `:`, backtick and Unicode dashes (U+2010/2011/2013) remain acceptable left neighbours, so `path/to/surface: sparq-core`, `meta.crates: ...` or `tool‑surface:` (U+2011) still parse as a T0 declaration.
nonblocking_findings.suggestion: If maintainers want it tighter, widen to something like `(?<![\w\-/.\u2010-\u2015])`; not required — this is strictly narrower than the pre-patch behaviour and over-tightening risks rejecting real fields.

nonblocking_findings.finding: The `classify(...) == ([], "")` half of the negative test also depends on T2 `_bd_derive` -> bd-to-issues.derive_areas declining two-crate bodies. That module is not in this packet, so a future T2 change can red this test for reasons unrelated to the T0 boundary. The `TA.declared_areas(...) == []` half is the boundary-specific assertion and is correctly present.

No fixture pins the single-crate prose case (`the tool-surface: sparq-core mapping ...` naming one crate). Such an issue now falls out of T0 into T1/T2 and may still be labelled with lower-trust evidence rather than staying parked. The docstring is honest that the two-crate shape is what makes these fixtures end in ([], ""), but the general framing is broader than what is asserted.

Vacuity check runs after the leaked/missed assertEqual, so a genuine leak masks the vacuity diagnostic; and the second check compares lengths only, so a helper returning duplicated or mis-scoped rows could in principle keep the arithmetic green (the realistic mutants are caught by the leaked/missed assertions and by the partial-partition control).
nonblocking_findings.suggestion: Optionally assert rule-id sets (disjoint union) instead of counts, and/or call the vacuity helper first.

nonblocking_findings.finding: Fixtures hardcode live workspace crate names (sparq-core, sparq-mpc, sparq-py) via crate_names(); a crate rename reds them. Consistent with existing tests in this file and arguably desirable.
The T0 prose test lives in TestRuleTableHygiene although T0 precedes the rule table; the added file-header comment explains the routing-around rationale. Naming/placement nit only.

Pre-existing asymmetry unchanged by this patch: `crates?` accepts the plural but `surface` has no `surfaces?`, so `surfaces: sparq-core` is not a declaration. Out of scope; noted only so it is not mistaken for a regression.

control_assessment.summary: Reported controls are well-targeted and discriminating; each ran 47 tests with 0 errors and failed through assertions, consistent with a suite that still imports cleanly under every mutant. Not independently executed by me.
discrimination: remove-left-boundary and word-boundary-hyphen-inert both red exactly test_a_declaration_shaped_string_in_prose_is_not_a_declaration; the `\b` variant is the load-bearing control because only the `tool-surface:` fixture distinguishes `\b` from `(?<![\w-])` — it proves the hyphen in the character class is not decorative.

disable-declaration `(?!)` reds test_a_real_declaration_still_reaches_t0 plus pre-existing T0/diagnostic tests, so the negative test cannot be satisfied by simply breaking the field — the over-tightening direction is pinned.

empty-title/empty-text partitions red both scope properties via the assertGreater(checked, 0) leg; partial-title-partition ([:1]) passes that leg and reds via the sum leg, so both independent checks in the new helper are separately exercised.
The disable-declaration fallout also demonstrates the #6473 diagnostic tests (TestTriageAreaDiagnostics) genuinely exercise the T0 path, i.e. they were present and live in the control runs.
gaps: No control removing only `-` from the class (behaviourally subsumed by the `\b` control, since `(?<!\w)` and `\b` coincide on these fixtures).
No control for a helper returning duplicate/mis-scoped rules (the length-only sum check would not catch it).

No control touching the unchanged write path (apply_row bare-unpark guard, #6473 unknown-label zero-write guard) — appropriate for this patch's scope, but it means those remain covered only by the pre-existing suite.
